newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-TUIGAMALA PERSONIFIES CURRENT RUGBY CHAOS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TUIGAMALA PERSONIFIES CURRENT RUGBY CHAOS.

text.p: Nobody personifies the current chaos in rugby better than giant Polynesian Va'aiga Tuigamala.

Tuigamala played rugby union for New Zealand. Then he transferred to the league code with Wigan. Currently he is on a four-match union contract with Wasps before returning to Wigan. On Tuesday he played his first union international for his native Western Samoa.
Although he did not score a try, Tuigamala's penetrative running and intelligent ball distribution led directly to three of Western Samoa's five tries as they overran Ireland 40-25 at Lansdowne Road.
But what does the future now hold?
"I'll fulfil the rest of my contract at Wasps then go back to league at Wigan and see how things go there," said an emotional Tuigamala after the Ireland match.
"I really don't know what will happen in future. Rugby union is a funny world these days."
Tuigamala has made at least one new fan.
Western Samoan coach, Bryan Williams, himself a famous All Black back in the 1970s was full of praise for his lastest cap.
"Va'aiga is a big influence," Williams said. "But it was not just his initial input into the game.
"Havng him around the last few days has been great. He is very confident, very mature and very experienced and made a big input into our performance."
Tuesday was an emotional night for the Samoan.

"Today was a very unique occasion for me, because it was the first time I was able to play for my native country in a rugby test," he said. "This is probably the proudest moment I have ever had as a Polynesian.
"Like I was saying before the match, I was hoping this would help Polynesian people get the recognition they deserve, and it was a big honour to be able to take part."
Tuigamala said he would encourage other members of the Western Samoan squad to play club rugby in England.
"It's a way they can broaden their horizons and can help them develop as players," he said.
Tuigamala was in Western Samoa's rugby league World Cup squad last year and had not played rugby union for three years prior to his appearance in Dublin.

He had played against Ireland once before, as an All Black in Dunedin in 1992. He toured Ireland with the 1989 All Blacks as a promising 20-year-old when he played against three Irish provincial sides.
Tuigamala's decision to switch to rugby league came as something of a surprise, but in retrospect it proved the making of Tuigamala as a rugby player.
He had been increasingly criticised in New Zealand as being more threatening than effective and professional trainers soon discovered that he was carrying far too much weight.
His fitness improved dramatically, his ball skills developed and at the age of 27 he is now at the peak of his considerable skills. Whichever code he represents.
